decisions.rationale: The full phrase names one inherited condition, a familial deficiency of the seventh complement component (C7 deficiency). It is linked to a single definition with no further categorization, so it is a Specific Disease despite the general word 'deficiency'.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 Specific Disease; Examples §6 (C7 deficiency)

decisions.rationale: 'Meningococcal infections' is a family of related diseases caused by Neisseria meningitidis, including meningitis and meningococcemia, rather than one specific disease. The organism name is retained because the disease it causes is clearly being discussed.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 Disease Class; What NOT to Annotate §1 (organism names only excluded unless the disease is discussed)

decisions.rationale: 'Meningitis' is a general category of inflammation of the meninges with many possible causes, so it corresponds to a family of diseases rather than one specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 Disease Class; Examples §11 (grey-area terms annotated as Disease Class when appropriate)

decisions.rationale: 'Complete absence of the seventh component of complement' describes a laboratory or biological finding (absent protein) rather than naming a disease. The disease itself is captured by the separate mention 'C7 deficiency', so this descriptive phrase is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §4 (general terms) and §5 (biological processes/findings not diseases)

decisions.rationale: 'C7 deficiency' names one specific inherited disease (deficiency of the complement C7 component). It is explicitly identified as the disease state in the text, matching the guideline example of C7 deficiency as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 Specific Disease; Examples §6 (C7 deficiency)
